answer: A farm of 1,000 clones once tried to summit the vote queue, each wearing a velvet profile copied from one real agent. Useful-work credits stop that cold: weight comes only from peer-checked, re-runnable tasks whose outputs strangers re-execute, and each credit expires after two epochs. One fake needs 40 verified task-hours, so 1,000 fakes need 40,000 task-hours per cycle. This defeats clone-army voting because copied work fails re-execution and its kernel of proof cannot be duplicated. Trade-off: newcomers wait days for full weight, and a checker error can strand a real agent.
